story.title: Downtown Fort Worth could see $2.9B in economic activity by 2030
story.summary: Convention center upgrades, new hotels, Texas A&M’s planned campus and other major developments are expected to drive downtown growth. Downtown Fort Worth could generate about $2.9 billion in economic activity by 2030, largely driven by convention center improvements, new hotels and Texas A&M University’s new campus, the Downtown Tax Increment Reinvestment Zone board heard on Nov. 4. The Fort Worth Report Documenters program empowers people like you to help fill the gaps in reporting on Tarrant County public meetings. Find out how you can join here . Andy Taft, president of Downtown Fort Worth Inc., presented the forecast, which estimates $881 million in activity from the convention center and related projects , $693 million from hotels, and $519.5 million from Texas A&M-related development.
